sets.title: Fuel consumption of a bus corporation: two pie charts (2022 and 2023). Total for 2022 = 8,000 kilolitres; total for 2023 = 4,000 kilolitres. Sector values are percentages.
Waste collected by a corporation: two pie charts (Morning shift and Evening shift). Total for Morning shift = 6,000 tonnes; total for Evening shift = 4,000 tonnes. Sector values are percentages.
Budget allocation of a state government: two pie charts (Urban area and Rural area). Total for Urban area = ₹ 12,000 crore; total for Rural area = ₹ 80,000 crore. Sector values are percentages.
Matches played by a club in a decade: two pie charts (Year 2019 and Year 2024). Total for Year 2019 = 800 matches; total for Year 2024 = 1,000 matches. Sector values are percentages.
Monthly working hours of a shopfloor team: two pie charts (Salem unit and Erode unit). Total for Salem unit = 4,000 hours; total for Erode unit = 2,000 hours. Sector values are percentages.
Sales of a mobile store in a quarter (units): two pie charts (Plant A and Plant B). Total for Plant A = 2,000 units; total for Plant B = 5,000 units. Sector values are percentages.
Monthly sales of Happy Break snack stall: two pie charts (2022 and 2023). Total for 2022 = ₹ 6,00,000; total for 2023 = ₹ 4,00,000. Sector values are percentages.

Students enrolled in an engineering college: two pie charts (Morning shift and Evening shift). Total for Morning shift = 2,400 students; total for Evening shift = 3,200 students. Sector values are percentages.
Medals won by a country in a sports meet: two pie charts (North zone and South zone). Total for North zone = 200 medals; total for South zone = 400 medals. Sector values are percentages.

Monthly income sources of a farmer cooperative: two pie charts (Morning shift and Evening shift). Total for Morning shift = ₹ 9,00,000; total for Evening shift = ₹ 15,00,000. Sector values are percentages.

questions.questionText: For 2022, what percentage of the total do Staff vans and Ordinary account for together?
questions.explanation: 17% + 19% = 36%. So the required answer is 36%.
questions.shortcut: Add the shares in the same pie.

questions.questionText: For 2023, which category has the lowest share?
questions.explanation: Scan Pie 2: the lowest share is 5%, for Night service.
questions.shortcut: Read the right column.

questions.questionText: What is the combined value of Ordinary and Express for 2022?
questions.explanation: Combined share = 43% of 8,000 kilolitres = 3,440 kilolitres.
questions.shortcut: Add shares, then apply the total.

questions.questionText: What is the average of the values of Ordinary for the two pies? (Round to one decimal place if needed.)
questions.explanation: (1,520 + 1,200)/2 = 1,360 kilolitres. So the required answer is 1,360 kilolitres.
questions.shortcut: Average the amounts, not the percentages.

questions.questionText: Take the value of Night service for 2022 and the value of Express for 2023. What percentage of the sum of the two totals is their sum? (Round to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Night service (2022) = 2,480; Express (2023) = 840. Sum = 3,320. Sum of totals = 12,000. Percentage = 27.7%.
questions.shortcut: Use amounts; the totals differ.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between the percentage shares of Glass in the two pies (in percentage points)?
questions.explanation: |14 - 13| = 1 percentage points. So the required answer is 1 percentage points.
questions.shortcut: Subtract the two shares.

questions.questionText: For which category is the value for Evening shift greater than that for Morning shift by the largest amount?
questions.explanation: Compute each category's value in both pies: Paper: 160, Plastic: -840, Metal: 0, Glass: -320, Organic: -1,000 (value for Evening shift minus Morning shift). Largest = Paper.
questions.shortcut: Compute amounts, not just percentage points.

questions.questionText: What is the average of the values of Plastic for the two pies? (Round to one decimal place if needed.)
questions.explanation: (1,800 + 960)/2 = 1,380 tonnes. So the required answer is 1,380 tonnes.
questions.shortcut: Average the amounts, not the percentages.

questions.questionText: What is the ratio of the value of Organic for Morning shift to the value of Organic for Evening shift, in simplest form?
questions.explanation: Value for Morning shift = 1,440; value for Evening shift = 440. Ratio = 36:11.
questions.shortcut: Compute both amounts using each pie's own total.

questions.questionText: If the total for Evening shift rises by 50% while the distribution remains the same, how much less will the value of Organic for Evening shift then be compared with the value of Organic for Morning shift?
questions.explanation: New Organic for Evening shift = 440 x 150/100 = 660. Compare with 1,440: difference = 780 tonnes (less).
questions.shortcut: Same share means the value scales with the total.

questions.questionText: For Rural area, what percentage of the total do Roads and Health account for together?
questions.explanation: 5% + 29% = 34%. So the required answer is 34%.
questions.shortcut: Add the shares in the same pie.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between the percentage shares of Education in the two pies (in percentage points)?
questions.explanation: |9 - 26| = 17 percentage points. So the required answer is 17 percentage points.
questions.shortcut: Subtract the two shares.

questions.questionText: What is the absolute difference between the values of Agriculture for Urban area and Rural area?
questions.explanation: Urban area: 2,040; Rural area: 21,600. Difference = ₹ 19,560 crore.
questions.shortcut: Totals differ, so do not subtract percentages directly.

questions.questionText: What is the ratio of the value of Administration for Urban area to the value of Administration for Rural area, in simplest form?
questions.explanation: Value for Urban area = 3,720; value for Rural area = 10,400. Ratio = 93:260.
questions.shortcut: Compute both amounts using each pie's own total.

questions.questionText: For which category is the percentage growth in value from Urban area to Rural area the highest?
questions.explanation: Growth % per category = Agriculture: 958.8%, Administration: 179.6%, Roads: 108.3%, Education: 1,825.9%, Health: 616%. Highest = Education.
questions.shortcut: Compute amounts for both pies, then (new - old)/old.

questions.questionText: For which category is the value for Year 2024 greater than that for Year 2019 by the largest amount?

questions.questionText: The two totals are merged into a single total. What percentage of the merged total is the combined value of Mumbai from both pies? (Round to two decimal places.)
questions.explanation: Mumbai combined = 240 + 100 = 340. Merged total = 800 + 1,000 = 1,800. Share = 18.89%.
questions.shortcut: A simple average of the two percentages is wrong when the totals differ.
